counterargs.read: Today's tape is a genuine, broad-based relief rally following a hike that landed as a bounded, largely-priced-in outcome -- the Korea gate flip and vol breakdown are real, confirmable signals, not noise. But the underlying policy stance is tighter than it was a week ago, and the real-yield grind (DFII5) hasn't paused. This reads as short-term conditions improving within a structurally restrictive backdrop -- consistent with the existing 'short-term Improving / long-term Restrictive' read -- rather than a full regime change. The next genuine test is the Sep 22-24 coupon auction trio, which will show whether the weak Sep 15 20Y demand mix was an isolated wobble or the start of something worse.

transmission.bottom_line: Today reads as a relief rally into Tuesday's FOMC hike (+25bp to 3.75-4.00%): oil's sharp reversal, easing VIX, and two exceptionally strong backfilled Treasury reopenings (10Y, 30Y) offset some of the concern from the weak Sep 15 20Y print.
